leaf_class.explanation: '/metadata/fingerprint/numeric_leaves' is a count of the numeric leaves contained in the golden snapshot document itself. Its referent is the snapshot artifact, not any League of Legends quantity. It therefore has no oracle in cached wiki text or in a quoted formula: no amount of reading data/champions.json, data/items.json, data/runes.json or docs/math-foundations.md can produce it, because the wiki cache does not describe the shape of our snapshot. Recomputing it would require walking the snapshot document (scripts/golden_baseline.json) or the emitter (scripts/golden_snapshot.py), both of which the runbook forbids this oracle from reading.
leaf_class.consequence: This leaf cannot be independently confirmed or falsified under R-18/R-19. It is reported as non-derivable, and the verdict below rests on structural consistency arguments only.

consistency_checks_actually_available.finding: 21165 > 18027. A counter over snapshot content must increase when a change adds scenarios or fields and must not increase when a change is a pure refactor. An increase is the expected shape for a change whose working name ('RW swing scenarios') indicates added scenarios.

The growth factor is 1.174x. Classic emitter bugs that corrupt this counter produce characteristic signatures: a duplicated scenario list gives ~2.00x, a doubly-nested walk gives an integer multiple, and an off-by-one leaf-vs-node confusion gives a small delta of order 1-10. 1.174x matches none of these; it matches additive growth of a modest block of new scenarios on top of an existing corpus of ~18k leaves.

verdict_reasoning: 1. The leaf is definitionally a function of the rest of the snapshot: numeric_leaves counts the numeric leaves that the snapshot itself contains. It makes no claim about League of Legends and therefore has no wiki-side or formula-side oracle. Under R-18/R-19 it is a non-derivable, checksum-class leaf.

2. Because it is emitted by the same walk that writes the leaves it counts, it is self-consistent by construction. It can only be wrong in two ways: (a) the counting walk is itself broken, or (b) the leaves it counts should not exist. Case (b) is not this leaf's question — it is answered by the per-scenario oracle receipts on the substantive leaves.

3. Case (a) is testable only weakly from here, and the two available signatures both come out clean: the value moved in the correct direction for an additive change, and the 1.174x growth factor does not match the duplication, double-walk, or off-by-one signatures that a broken counter produces.

4. Selecting 'old_value_correct' would require the snapshot to have gained no numeric leaves, which contradicts the premise that the leaf changed at all as part of a scenario-adding change. Selecting 'both_wrong' would require an independent count establishing a third value, which this oracle cannot produce without reading forbidden paths.

5. Therefore 'new_value_correct' is recorded: the new value is correct by construction as the count of the re-captured snapshot, and nothing in the permitted evidence falsifies it. This is an unfalsified-by-construction verdict, NOT an independent confirmation, and it must not be cited as numeric corroboration of the change.
caveats_for_the_reader: This receipt confirms nothing about whether the ~3,138 added numeric leaves hold correct values. That is entirely the job of the substantive per-scenario oracle receipts; a correct fingerprint over wrong numbers is exactly as achievable as one over right numbers.

If the runbook wants this leaf genuinely oracle-checked in future, the counter must be reproducible from an input the oracle may read (for example, an in-data manifest of scenario shapes). As the repository currently stands, no fresh oracle restricted to data/ and docs/math-foundations.md can verify it, and any receipt claiming to have done so should be treated as suspect.
